svg.title: Making a room your own
svg.desc: Original family-manga illustration: room, related to Making a room your own.

text.tspan: A good way to arrange a room combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid plan nor complete
improvisation is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use. Consider how we keep keys in a bowl beside the door. The
benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents avoidable confusion, leaving attention available for the activity itself rather than for problems that could
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: small personal choices make a space feel familiar. In this situation, we place a favourite photograph where
we can see it from our chair. A decision can be convenient for one person while creating difficulty for another, so its value depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting point; attention to other people keeps it
responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the experience, rather than by how closely events follow the original plan.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example. Conclude by connecting the two
reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an experience of your own.
Explain the meaning before looking at the model answer. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that giving
everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use and that small personal choices make a space feel familiar. One example is that we keep keys in a bowl
